note: Working definitions written for this inquiry.

terms.definition: Change in what higher education is (its functions, form, boundaries, legitimacy and mandate) associated with digital and automated technologies; distinct from digitalization IN higher education, which concerns tools used inside existing structures.
The underlying logic of a role, practice, institution or mandate persists.
The underlying logic or actor is displaced or replaced.
New forms or media are added and authority is rearranged while existing forms persist.
Separating functions (for example teaching, assessment, credentialing) that were provided together, and later recombining them in new arrangements.
Individual roles and practices; the institution as organisation; societal mandate and the knowledge system.
A development that is positive at one level and negative at another.
Service, extension, engagement, knowledge transfer and societal impact; the term varies by period and tradition.
Higher education delivered at a distance through post, broadcast, telecommunications or networks; includes combined-format universities and open universities.
A campus university that also teaches external or distance students.
A distance-teaching institution with open admission; the UK Open University (1969) is the best-known example.
The surrounding set of academies and societies, journals, publishers, conferences, indexes, libraries, repositories, funders and platforms within which HEIs operate. Working label only.
Turning institutional data, content or infrastructure into assets from which platforms extract rent; used in critical platform studies.
Growing dependence of institutional functions on commercial platforms and vendors.
Frameworks describing coordination among universities, industry, state (and civil society).
Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable (research data principles, 2016).
Declarations and coalitions on responsible research assessment (2013, 2015, 2022).
A model that places societies or institutions on a single developmental ladder; not used here, and reported only with its critiques.
Evidence labels used across the package; see vocabularies.json.
Historical patterns are used to frame questions, not to predict outcomes.
